Part 3 · Are the safeguards enough?

Are the safeguards enough? LOPA, groups and the report

Part 3 · the plan

From a row to a number

  1. The LOPA quantitiesfrequencies, probabilities, the target
  2. Two equationsunmitigated, then mitigated frequency
  3. Row N5.1 workeddoes it meet the target?
  4. Groups, workshop, hand-inbeyond one row

Full edition · LOPA

The quantities on a LOPA row

$f_{IE}$
initiating-event frequency, one per cause
1/yr
$P_{EN},\ P_{CM}$
enabling condition, conditional modifier probabilities
–
$PFD_j$
probability of failure on demand of IPL $j$
–
$f_{unmit},\ f_{mit}$
consequence frequency without, with the IPLs
1/yr
$TEL$
tolerable event likelihood for severity $S$
1/yr
$RRR,\ RRF$
required risk reduction, risk reduction factor
–

Library values are teaching defaults in the CCPS style.

Derivation · step 1 of 2

How often does the consequence start?

$f_{unmit}=\Big(\sum_i f_{IE,i}\Big)\prod_k P_{EN,k}\prod_m P_{CM,m}$causes add; each condition must also hold, so multiply
$P_{CM}$: ignition, person presentthe event must also harm someone

Derivation · step 2 of 2

How often do all the layers fail too?

$f_{unmit}=\big(\sum f_{IE}\big)\prod P_{EN}\prod P_{CM}$
$f_{mit}=f_{unmit}\prod_j PFD_j$independent layers must all fail on demand
$RRF=\dfrac{f_{mit}}{TEL},\quad RRR=\dfrac{TEL}{f_{mit}}$RRF > 1 means another layer is needed

When $f_{mit}\le TEL$ both read "None": the row meets the target.

Example 1 · problem statement · read first

EXAMPLE 1Overpressure of the liquid-full column (N5.1)

Node N5, Pressure MORE, S 4. The raffinate outlet is blocked while both pumps run. Initiating events: PV-108 or its positioner fails closed; PIC-108 fails low and closes PV-108; a downstream block valve is closed in error, each 0.1 /yr. Modifiers: ignition 0.3, person present 0.5. IPLs: PSHH-108 (SIF-01) and PSV-108; the PI-108 alarm gets no credit. Is the risk tolerable?

Example 1 · solution

EXAMPLE 1The two layers bring it under the target

$f_{mit}=\big(\sum f_{IE}\big)\prod P_{CM}\prod PFD_j$
$f_{unmit}=0.3\times0.15=0.045\ \text{yr}^{-1}$three causes of 0.1; modifiers 0.3 × 0.5
$f_{mit}=0.045\times0.0101\times0.01=4.55\times10^{-6}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$PSHH-108 and PSV-108 must both fail

Interactive · change the layers

Which layer carries the row?

Set either PFD to 1 (layer removed): f_mit rises a hundredfold and the row needs another layer.

Interactive · change the severity of N5.1

The target tightens tenfold per severity step

With f_mit 4.55 × 10⁻⁶ /yr, N5.1 meets S1 to S4 but would need another layer at S5.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Causes add, conditions and layers multiply.
  • N5.1: PSHH-108 and PSV-108 bring it under the S 4 target.
  • Groups total rows that share a consequence.
  • The study .json is the hand-in.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Keep only deviations that can happen on the node.

2

Judge consequences with no credit for safeguards.

3

Link safeguards so one edit reaches every row.

4

Run the ▶ OTS test before trusting a safeguard.

5

Use LOPA when R is High: count only independent layers.
